questiontext.text:
The arrow on the grid goes from P to Q.

[[jsxgraph width="440px" height="360px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-0.6, 7.6, 9.6, -0.6], axis: false, grid: false, keepAspectRatio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}); var gl = {strokeColor: '#d0d0d0', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}; for (var gx = 0; gx <= 9; gx++) { b.create('segment', [[gx, 0], [gx, 7]], gl); } for (var gy = 0; gy <= 7; gy++) { b.create('segment', [[0, gy], [9, gy]], gl); } var tx = {fixed: true, highlight: false, useMathJax: false, fontSize: 13}; var lab = {fixed: true, highlight: false, useMathJax: false, fontSize: 16}; for (var tk = 0; tk <= 9; tk++) { b.create('text', [tk - 0.15, 0 - 0.35, String(tk)], tx); } for (var tk2 = 1; tk2 <= 7; tk2++) { b.create('text', [0 - 0.5, tk2, String(tk2)], tx); } var ar = {strokeColor: '#1f4e9c', strokeWidth: 3, lastArrow: {type: 2, size: 5}, fixed: true, highlight: false}; var po = {fixed: true, highlight: false, size: 2, fillColor: '#000000', strokeColor: '#000000', withLabel: false}; b.create('point', [{#x0#}, {#y0#}], po); b.create('point', [{#x1#}, {#y1#}], po); b.create('arrow', [[{#x0#}, {#y0#}], [{#x1#}, {#y1#}]], ar); b.create('text', [{#x0#} + 0.15, {#y0#} + 0.35, 'P'], lab); b.create('text', [{#x1#} + 0.15, {#y1#} + 0.35, 'Q'], lab); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

(a) Write \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\) as a column vector.

generalfeedback.text:
The top number is the move across and the bottom number the move up. Moves left or down are negative.

(a) From \(P({@x0@},\,{@y0@})\) the arrow goes \({@abs(a)@}\) [[if test="is(a>0)"]]right[[else]]left[[/if]] and \({@abs(b)@}\) [[if test="is(b>0)"]]up[[else]]down[[/if]] to \(Q({@x1@},\,{@y1@})\), so \(\overrightarrow{PQ} = {@ta@}\).

(b) \(\overrightarrow{QP}\) goes the other way, from Q back to P, so both signs change: \(\overrightarrow{QP} = -\overrightarrow{PQ} = {@tb@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Vectors: column vectors from a grid

Grade 12 CBE Essential 2.2: Write the column vector of an arrow drawn on a grid, and of the reverse arrow.

Essential

You counted the squares but left out the signs. A move left or down is negative.

falsefeedback.text: Check your vector on the grid: it takes \(P({@x0@},\,{@y0@})\) to \(({@zE[1]@},\,{@zE[2]@})\), which is not Q. Count the squares from P to Q: across first, then up or down.

truefeedback.text: That is \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\). \(\overrightarrow{QP}\) goes the other way, from Q back to P, so both signs change.

The top number is the move across and the bottom number the move up. From P the arrow goes \({@abs(a)@}\) [[if test="is(a>0)"]]right[[else]]left[[/if]] and \({@abs(b)@}\) [[if test="is(b>0)"]]up[[else]]down[[/if]].

falsefeedback.text: Check your vector on the grid: it takes \(Q({@x1@},\,{@y1@})\) to \(({@zF[1]@},\,{@zF[2]@})\), not back to P. \(\overrightarrow{QP}\) is the reverse of \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\): change the sign of both components.
